newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power flat to lower amid outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power flat to lower amid outages.

text.p: Western U.S. spot power prices were flat to slightly lower as expectations for cooler weather in the Northwest were offset by power line restrictions, market sources said Friday.
"Some marketers got caught long and had to dump energy (in the Northwest)," said one trader.

Monday between 0630 and 1800 PDT, southbound transmissions on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie were limited for planned maintenance work to 2,000 megawatts (MW), compared with a usual rating of 3,200 MW, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said.
BPA continued to refrain from offering surplus power during peak demand hours through the weekend and Sunday.

Absence of the federal power marketing agency was attributed to forecasts for colder weather, ongoing curtailments at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant, outage of a 805 MW turbine at the Grand Coulee dam and outage of a 500 kilovolt transmission line running to the Canadian border.
Market sources said the continued lack of peak offers was not really a surprise since BPA cannot count on having these problems resolved by Monday.
